info.text:
In 2020, stocks fell 34% in 33 days. Here's what happens in a crash.
The S&P 500 fell from 3,386.15 (Feb 19, 2020) to 2,237.40 (Mar 23, 2020), then closed at a record 3,389.78 on Aug 18, 2020. Getting back took a 51% climb.
Circuit breakers: a 7% or 13% S&P 500 drop before 3:25 p.m. ET pauses US stock trading for 15 minutes; 20% closes it for the day. They triggered 4 times in March 2020.
Margin example: $10,000 of stock with $5,000 borrowed drops 34% to $6,600, leaving $1,600 of equity (24.2%), under FINRA's 25% minimum, so a margin call.
Sources: NYSE; SEC Investor.gov; FINRA Rule 4210; NPR, CNN (Aug 18, 2020). Past recoveries don't predict future ones.
News and education, not financial advice.
